newsitem.title: USA: St Paul Bancorp eyes expense control.
newsitem.headline: St Paul Bancorp eyes expense control.

text.p: St Paul Bancorp Inc intends to focus on expense controls, chairman and chief executive Joseph Scully said Thursday at a Piper Jaffray investment conference.

He noted that general and administrative expenses for the first nine months of 1996 rose seven percent to $72.5 million from $67.5 million in the first nine months of 1995. For the third quarter ended September 30 general and administrative expenses rose 10 percent to $24.8 million.

The company's third-quarter statement with its earnings said advertising expenditures and occupancy and office expenses showed the largest percentage increases in both the quarter and the nine months.

In an interview after his presentation, Scully said he anticipates that investments in technology will help bring expenses down. He noted that starting up new technologies such as telephone banking requires higher outlays in the beginning. He did not cite any numerical goals for cutting costs.
St Paul operates 17 in-store branches. Scully said it costs four to eight times as much to open a conventional branch compared to a supermarket branch.
Chicago-based St. Paul Bancorp is the corporate parent of St. Paul Federal Bank for Savings, the largest independent savings institution in Illinois.

Scully also said that St Paul Bancorp considers stock repurchases an alternative to doing dilutive acquisitions. The company currently has a 900,000 share repurchase program which was approved by the board of directors three months ago. The company had 18.1 million shares outstanding on September 30, 1996, the end of the third quarter.
